text:
monitoring-bot: ALERT: apiserver 5xx and etcd leader churn detected in us-west1 controlplane. spike started ~2026-05-01T11:59:58Z, see dashboard https://monitoring.redwood/alerts/CP-1855
arjun: noticed Dedicated GPU node provisioning errors — pod create returning 503, nodes stuck in "Provisioning" state.
maya: looking... controller-manager shows heavy retries and node-status RPC failures. logs:
```
I0501 11:59:58 controller.go:210] sync gpu-provisioner default/gpu-node-01
E0501 12:00:00 controller.go:218] Post "https://apiserver.kube-system.svc:6443/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods": 503 Service Unavailable
W0501 12:00:01 node_controller.go:345] failed to update node status: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection reset by peer
```
tom: any control-plane workflows/maintenance around then? cc @infra
jessica: no apiserver deploys from CI in last 12h. scheduled etcd compaction ran at 11:58 UTC (regular weekly job).
luis: network telemetry shows NAT gateway egress packet drops/err spikes at 11:59 across controlplane subnets in us-west1. p99 RTT to etcd rose ~200-300ms briefly.
arjun: etcd debug logs show leader flip-flopping exactly in that window:
```
2026-05-01T11:59:58Z etcdserver: leader changed: 5 -> 2
2026-05-01T12:00:03Z etcdserver: leader changed: 2 -> 5
2026-05-01T12:00:09Z etcdserver: lease renew timeout
```
maya: hypothesis: compaction caused IO/CPU pressure + NAT egress saturation -> raft timeouts -> leader churn -> apiserver 5xx -> controller-manager errors -> GPU provisioner fails.
om: @oncall can we interrupt compaction or add NAT capacity quickly? compaction during noisy network is risky.
oncall: oncall here. pausing compaction mid-run is not ideal but better than prolonged control-plane outages. Pausing scheduler now and scaling NAT (added IPs + extra NAT instances). following runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/cp/compaction
jessica: compaction paused at 12:05 UTC. NAT scale requested 12:06 UTC.
arjun: post-pause metrics show etcd leader stabilized; apiserver 5xx dropped from ~40% to ~4% within ~90s.
monitoring-bot: ALERT RESOLVED: apiserver error rate back to normal. Incident ticket: https://pm.redwood/incidents/CP-2026-05-01
maya: follow-ups to track:
- stagger etcd compaction per-region (avoid global sync)
- add NAT autoscale for controlplane subnets (trigger on egress drops/RTT)
- compaction job short-circuit if controlplane RTT > threshold
- combined alert: compaction job + high RTT -> auto-pause

tom: also harden GPU provisioner to tolerate transient 5xxs: smarter retry/backoff and treat some 5xx as retryable with capped TTL.
luis: I'll open PR for NAT autoscale + dashboard panels for controlplane egress.
jessica: I'll own postmortem writeup + attach timeline logs (etcd compaction start, NAT drop, leader events, apiserver 5xx, controller-manager errors). assigning CP-ops.
arjun: operational mitigation suggestion: create a small canary Dedicated GPU pool in a secondary region for immediate failover capacity.
maya: agree; also throttle compaction IO and add QoS so it doesn't saturate disk during peak windows.
om: updated runbook with detection for compaction+RTT combo and recommended auto-pause thresholds.
oncall: mitigation steps executed. monitoring to watch for 24h; incident remains open for postmortem items.
jessica: postmortem ETA EOD tomorrow, owner @jessica. tagging CP-ops.
arjun: thanks all. watch provisioning queues for next 2 hours. :thumbsup:
